# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.13
# The SSH jail logs with a 30-byte prefix: the kernel keeps 29 — silently —
# so every line reads "FW-INPUT-DROP-SSH-BRUTEFORCE:" and the fail2ban filter
# keyed on "FW-INPUT-DROP-SSH-BRUTEFORCE: " never matches. The web log's
# prefix fits (exactly 29 bytes with its space).
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m recent --update --seconds 60 --hitcount 5 --name ssh -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "FW-INPUT-DROP-SSH-BRUTEFORCE: "
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m recent --update --seconds 60 --hitcount 5 --name ssh -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m recent --set --name ssh -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -m comment --comment "public HTTPS" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m limit --limit 5/min -j LOG --log-prefix "FW-INPUT-DROP-DEFAULT-POLICY "
COMMIT
